featured_reviews.name: Prashant “Paddy” Demello
featured_reviews.review_text:
Sai Veg World is one of those rare places that holds a lot of nostalgia while still continuing to evolve, and that’s exactly what keeps me coming back. I have been visiting this place since its inception, back when this building used to be a post office in the early 2000s. Watching it transform into a popular vegetarian restaurant over the years has been quite a journey.

One thing I genuinely appreciate about Sai Veg World is that the management keeps experimenting with new ideas and concepts. They don’t remain stuck in one format, and you can clearly see the effort to improve and adapt with time. That willingness to try new things is something I really like about this place.

The menu offers plenty of variety, especially when it comes to snacks and quick bites. Whether you’re looking for a light breakfast, evening snacks, or a proper vegetarian meal, there’s always something to choose from. The South Indian dishes are the main attraction here and have never disappointed me. From dosas to idlis and other South Indian snacks, the taste has remained consistently good over the years, making it a reliable spot for a quick and satisfying meal.

It’s also a great place for a quick breakfast or snack stop, especially if you’re in the Goregaon East area. Service is generally efficient, and the place manages to handle regular crowd flow fairly well.

Overall, Sai Veg World continues to be a dependable vegetarian restaurant with a lot of variety, a strong South Indian focus, and a management team that keeps trying to innovate. A solid 4-star experience and a place I’d definitely recommend if you’re looking for good vegetarian food in Goregaon East.

featured_reviews.review_text:
Ratna Veg Restaurant in Goregaon West has become one of our regular breakfast spots after weekend gym workouts. It's a simple and reliable place to enjoy a satisfying South Indian breakfast without burning a hole in your pocket.

On my recent visit, I tried their Cheese Masala Dosa, and it was absolutely delicious. The dosa was crisp, generously filled, and had just the right amount of cheese without overpowering the traditional flavors. Definitely a must-try if you're visiting for breakfast.

Apart from South Indian dishes, they also offer a good variety of North Indian food, making it a convenient option for different cravings throughout the day. The service is usually quick, and the food is served fresh and hot.

The ambience is fairly average and nothing particularly fancy, but the quality of food makes up for it. If you're looking for a dependable place for a tasty breakfast or a casual meal with family and friends, Ratna Veg Restaurant is worth a visit.

Visited Sai Veg near Bagur Nagar Metro Station (right opposite Dmart), and I must say it’s a hidden gem for vegetarians. The ambience is simple, neat, and welcoming – nothing too fancy, but perfect for enjoying good food with family or friends.

We ordered quite a lot – Paneer Kulcha Masala, Paneer Satay, Paneer Tikka, Veg Biryani, Damy Ban Masala Dosa, Thatti Idli, and Mysore Masala Dosa. Every dish had its own flavor and felt freshly made. The paneer dishes were soft, well marinated, and very tasty. The dosas were crisp with the right balance of masala, and the Thatti Idli was super soft and comforting.

Service was quick and polite, and the portion sizes were generous compared to the price. It’s definitely value for money, especially if you’re looking for a pure veg place with lots of options.

Overall, a really good experience – tasty food, good variety, and a calm vibe. Highly recommended if you’re in the area and craving some hearty vegetarian food. 🌿✨

Overall, a solid place for good South Indian food in Goregaon.

featured_reviews.review_text:
A Golden Symphony of Mangoes – Mango Mania Brunch at Café Fleur, The Fern by Marriott

Our experience at Café Fleur was nothing short of a five-star celebration of mango magic—a brunch where every element, from the food to the service, shimmered in indulgence and warmth.

From the moment we stepped in, the ambience wrapped us in a cozy, elegant charm, setting the tone for what felt like a luxurious tropical escape. The hospitality elevated the experience even further—Ravindra, Vaibhav, Rishabh, and Vanshika ensured every moment flowed seamlessly, with attentive, warm, and genuinely thoughtful service.

The menu itself was a lavish canvas of global and Indian flavours, thoughtfully curated and beautifully executed  . From comforting soups to vibrant starters like Amritsari fish fry and hariyali aloo tikka, every dish was crafted to excite the palate. The live counters and mezze spreads added layers of interactive indulgence, while the mains—from rich Malwani curries to fragrant biryanis and Asian delicacies—offered something for every craving.

But what truly stole the spotlight was the celebration of mango in its most glorious forms. The salad section was a revelation—fresh, vibrant, and bursting with tropical brightness. Dishes like the spicy mango cucumber salad and mango-avocado creations were refreshing, zesty, and beautifully balanced, proving that mango can be as versatile as it is indulgent.

And then came the grand finale—the dessert spread. A breathtaking plethora of desserts in stunning shades of mango yellow, each one more irresistible than the last. From silky mango panna cotta and luscious mango mousse to decadent mango cheesecakes and traditional delights like aam ras and mango shrikhand—this was pure dessert heaven. Every bite was a celebration of the king of fruits, rich, fragrant, and utterly satisfying.

This brunch wasn’t just a meal—it was a mango-infused culinary journey, where every dish told a story of indulgence and creativity.

Five stars, without a doubt.
And yes… we’re already dreaming of our next visit.

featured_reviews.name: Krish Rachchh
featured_reviews.review_text:
I had an extremely disturbing and disappointing experience at Green Tadka, and it completely destroyed the image I had of this place.

When you choose a restaurant that looks decent and well-maintained, you naturally expect clean, hygienic food and professional standards. You believe that if you’re paying to eat at a “good” restaurant, your food will at least be safe. Unfortunately, that trust was completely broken here.

I ordered a dosa and found a dead mosquito inside it — absolutely disgusting and shocking. No customer should ever have to face something like this. It immediately makes you question what kind of hygiene standards they follow and what else might be happening behind the scenes.

What made things even more concerning is that the dosa wasn’t even prepared in a proper kitchen. It was being made openly in the restaurant area itself, exposed to the environment, customers walking around, and clearly insects as well. Watching food being prepared in such an unhygienic, open manner explains exactly how something like a mosquito could end up inside a dish. It shows a serious lack of food safety practices.

To make matters worse, I had already eaten a dosa from there earlier. Now I’m left wondering whether that one was safe or not, which is honestly disturbing.

The manager,did apologize, but then said something completely illogical — he told me not to pay for the previous dosa I had ordered. Waiving payment doesn’t fix a hygiene disaster. It felt more like an attempt to brush the issue under the carpet than to genuinely resolve it.

The manager, clearly did not know how to handle a serious customer complaint. Instead of responding calmly, professionally, and taking proper responsibility, he seemed confused and unprepared. His way of dealing with the situation felt careless and illogical, as if he was trying to avoid the issue rather than resolve it. Rather than reassuring the customer and offering a clear solution, he gave vague answers and excuses, which made the situation even more frustrating. A manager is supposed to lead, take accountability, and protect the restaurant’s standards — but in this case, there was a complete lack of professionalism and proper complaint handling.

When I asked for the owner’s contact number or email to know him about the situation so I could escalate the matter, I was told, “Owner gaon gaya hai.” No contact details, no proper complaint process, no accountability — just excuses.

A restaurant’s reputation is built on trust. Customers trust that the food they are served is prepared safely and hygienically. Here, not only was that trust broken, but the way the situation was handled afterward showed a complete lack of professionalism and concern for customer health.

I left feeling disgusted, shocked, and extremely disappointed.

This was one of the worst dining experiences I’ve ever had, and I would strongly advise others to think twice before eating here. No one should risk their health at a place that claims to be a quality restaurant but fails at the most basic standards of cleanliness and responsibility.

This is a major hygiene issue and poses a risk to customer health. I request a proper explanation of how such contamination occurred, details of the hygiene measures followed in food preparation, and assurance that corrective action will be taken to prevent this from happening again. I also request to speak with the owner or a senior authority, as the issue was not handled satisfactorily by the manager on duty,Please treat this matter seriously and respond at the earliest with a clear resolution..

I tried the veg bao here for the very first time, and I completely fell for it. Soft, flavorful, and perfectly balanced, it instantly became one of my new favorites on the menu. The service by the waiters was equally impressive. They were polite, attentive, and genuinely helpful throughout the visit. From guiding us with the menu to serving quickly and courteously, they made the dining experience smooth and enjoyable.

What I loved the most was the consistency – even after a decade of ordering, the taste and service inside the restaurant matched the same high standards I’ve always received at home. That kind of reliability is rare, and Greens definitely stands out because of it.

Overall, Greens Veg Restaurant is more than just a reliable option for delivery – it’s a wonderful place to dine in as well. With great food variety, excellent service, and a clean, well-maintained ambiance, it remains one of the best vegetarian restaurants in Malad West.

featured_reviews.name: Sachin Gupta
featured_reviews.review_text:
I recently visited Bhagwati Veg Restaurant and honestly, it was a very disappointing experience. The service was painfully slow, making the entire dining experience frustrating. On top of that, the pricing is absolutely unreasonable – it felt as if I was dining at a luxury Taj hotel rather than a casual outlet.

The "Veg Chopper Rice" in particular was shockingly overpriced for what they served. The portion was very small, and the taste and quality were extremely ordinary – nothing special at all to justify the sky-high cost. When you see the final bill, it really feels like you’ve been overcharged for items that are just average.

Overall, this place is not worth the price at all. There are far better restaurants in the nearby area that serve good food at much more affordable and genuine rates. Bhagwati Veg Restaurant gives the impression of cashing in by overcharging customers without delivering quality or value for money.

I would strongly recommend exploring other nearby options instead of wasting money here.
